content:
maya: Quick sync - cost observability flagged a retention explosion from traces with large baggage. Need to scope an approach that reduces spend without losing billing accuracy.

raj: Yep. Graph shows 3 tenants driving most bytes; they have verbose debug spans kept for 30d. Naive retention TTL cuts cost but breaks billing attribution in a few pipelines.

katie: I dug in. The problem is we currently decide sampling in the collector after enrichment. If we move sampling earlier we save bandwidth, but enrichment (which injects billing_key) runs later and sometimes never attaches.

maya: proposal: add a tiny signed attribution header at ingress with tenant_id + sketch flags (no user data). Edge sampler can use it to make early keep/drop decisions and still attribute cost.

tim: two alternatives: 1) sample at edge and carry header; 2) keep sampling after enrichment but add a cheaper pre-check that drops obviously-low-value traces. Both have tradeoffs.

ingest-bot: FYI: current enrichment SLA is 5s; late joins to billing table are happening ~0.5% of the time.

katie: thinking about fidelity metrics: we need sampling_precision (how often sampled traces map to same billing id post-enrich), attribution_gap_rate, and bytes_saved_pct. Also a per-tenant preview of estimated monthly savings.

maya: operational constraints: no PII in header, header size <64 bytes, backwards compatible with existing proxies. Security review required.

privacy-bot: flagged - header must NOT contain user identifiers. Recommend tenant GUID + HMAC signature. If team wants higher assurance, use KMS-signed token.

raj: sketch of the edge header (informal):

```
# ingress header (base64)
{ "t": "tenant-guid", "v": 1, "h": "hmac" }
```

katie: for implementation:
- make sampler library for proxies (lua/wasm) that reads header and decides on sampled=true/false
- emit sampled=true marker so downstream keeps full KV cache for that trace
- if enrichment later adds/changes billing key, emit an attribution_correction metric

maya: fallback policy: if no header present, collector can do a cheap heuristic (status code, latency, route) to avoid dropping all successful slow traces. Also keep a 48h grace window before truncating bodies without billing.

tim: canary plan:
- cohort A: 2% traffic, header-enabled early sampling
- cohort B: 2% traffic, header-disabled but collector-heuristic sampling
- monitor attribution_precision, billing_lookup_missing, retention_bytes, and error SLOs for 2 weeks

katie: add runbook: on billing_lookup_missing > 0.1% for 1h, pause sampling and increase retention for affected tenants.

raj: infra work: prototype sampler in proxy and a collector flag that honors sampled marker. I'll send a draft PR by Thu.

privacy-bot: note added - please prepare a 1-pager for security review focusing on header lifecycle and key rotation if using HMAC/KMS.

maya: next steps/action items:
- raj -> proxy sampler prototype (PR Thu)
- katie -> metrics + dashboard (cohort comparisons)
- tim -> privacy/ops note + runbook draft
- maya -> coordinate canary with release-war-room and billing team

katie: small ask: include lightweight checksum of span payload in header so if proxy drops body we can at least reconcile via checksum for billing claims. Not a blocker.

maya: good idea. keep it optional.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll post the canary kickoff in #release-war-room once PRs are green. :shipit:
